professionalBackground.title: Professional Background
paragraphs: Daniel Cohen is a Mathematics and Statistics professional with an M.A. in Statistics & Applied Mathematics from Hunter College (GPA 3.93), MBA in Finance & Investments from Baruch College — Zicklin School of Business (Finance GPA 4.00), and B.A. in Mathematics & Economics from Queens College — Magna Cum Laude, Arthur D. Gayer Memorial Award in Economics. He passed Society of Actuaries exams P/1, FM/2, and MFE, grounding his work in probability, financial mathematics, and quantitative risk thinking.

College-level teaching at Kingsborough Community College, Queens College, Pace University, and Yeshiva University — plus Business Statistics labs with Excel and current quantitative instruction at The Montfort Academy — strengthened clear communication of statistical ideas. That background supports analytics storytelling and stakeholder-facing interpretation; it complements, rather than replaces, his product and technical portfolio evidence.

analyticsAiTransition.title: Quantitative Analytics & Product Expansion
paragraphs: Daniel has expanded his mathematics, statistics, and finance foundation into quantitative analytics, AI evaluation, AI-assisted product development, and technical product work. The Daniel AI Suite — seven deployed Streamlit applications plus SQL and Excel workbooks — is deliberate proof: independent product ownership from problem framing through deployment.

Across the suite: product problem identification, prioritization, requirements, user workflows, architecture decisions, APIs and persistence, multi-user behavior, AI-assisted implementation, validation, debugging, recommendation systems, and AI output evaluation — with acceptance criteria and iteration from live usage.

Portfolio optimization, hypothesis testing, Monte Carlo simulation, ML projections, betting EV, epidemic modeling, and AI evaluator workflows extend the same quantitative foundation built through actuarial study, business statistics labs, and graduate statistics training — now packaged as interactive products recruiters can click through in minutes.
